title: Attorney General of Georgia

context.text: Neither candidate is an incumbent: Attorney General Chris Carr (R) ran for governor instead of seeking re-election.
Tanya Miller defeated Robert Trammell 84.6% to 15.4% in the May 19 Democratic primary; Brian Strickland defeated Bill Cowsert 71.6% to 28.4% in the May 19 Republican primary.
Atlanta News First's post-primary ballot rundown and The Green Papers list only Miller (D) and Strickland (R) for Attorney General.

candidates.name: Tanya Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 84.6%.

priorities.text: Enforcing the law and public safety: working with local prosecutors against violent crime, illegal guns, drugs and trafficking, and supporting diversion programs for nonviolent first-time offenders.
Defending Georgia's laws and Constitution, including protecting civil rights, fair elections and fighting public corruption.
Protecting consumers from scams, predatory lending and price gouging.

record.text: Says she introduced HB 1521 to prevent Ponzi schemes, HB 1520 to stop rent price-fixing by corporate landlords, and HB 733 on public participation in insurance rate setting, bills in the 2025-2026 General Assembly (her description in her candidate survey).

candidates.researchNotes: Bill descriptions and sponsorship come from her own survey and could not be checked against legis.ga.gov (blocked); HB 733 is a 2025-26 bill with committee action in February 2026. No direct statements on the guide's issue statements were found.

candidates.name: Brian Strickland
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary with 71.6%.

priorities.text: Affordability for families, including keeping corporate actors from cheating consumers and ensuring Georgians get the first opportunity to purchase homes.
Protecting vulnerable Georgians: cracking down on scams targeting seniors, identity theft, gangs and human trafficking.
Experience and independence from politics; he says more than 100 sheriffs, district attorneys and first-responder organizations have endorsed him.

record.text: Chairs the Georgia Senate Judiciary Committee (2025-26 session); describes in his candidate survey having written state laws on gangs and human trafficking.

candidates.researchNotes: Individual bills and roll-call votes were not itemized. No direct statements on the guide's issue statements were found.
